title: Subject-Verb Agreement with Prepositional Phrase

options.text: The bouquet of red roses smell wonderful.
The bouquet of red roses smells wonderful.
The bouquets of red rose smells wonderful.
The bouquet of red rose smell wonderful.

explanation: The singular subject is 'The bouquet' (not 'roses'). A singular subject requires the singular verb 'smells'.

title: Synonym Identification
statement: Choose the word most nearly opposite in meaning (Antonym) to 'EPHEMERAL':
explanation: 'Ephemeral' means lasting for a very short time. Its direct antonym is 'Permanent' (enduring/long-lasting).

title: Conditional Clause Error
statement: Find the incorrect part: 'If I was the Prime Minister (A) / of this country (B) / I would eradicate poverty (C) / No error (D)'
explanation: In hypothetical/unreal conditional statements (subjunctive mood), 'were' is used instead of 'was': 'If I were the Prime Minister...'

title: Meaning of Idiom
statement: What does the idiom 'Bite the bullet' mean?

options.text: To face a difficult or unpleasant situation with courage

explanation: 'Bite the bullet' means to bravely accept or endure an inevitable, difficult situation.
